source_text: hoc inter se foedus iniisse diabolum et Deum, ut quidquid perfunditur, Deus; quidquid nascitur, diabolus sibi vindicet: ea tamen lege - sicut dicis - ut ipsam commixtionem quam diabolus instituit, Deus obnoxia virtute fecundet
pass_a_gloss: This among himself foedus iniisse diabolum and God, so-that/as quidquid perfunditur, God; quidquid is-born, the-devil to-himself vindicet: she/it nevertheless by-the-law - as you-say - so-that/as ipsam mixing than/which the-devil instituit, God obnoxia by-virtue fecundet.

lemmas.lexica: LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: The devil and God have made this agreement between them: God is to claim whatever is washed, and the devil whatever is born. But on this condition: God, by a power subject to another, is to make fruitful the very sexual union that the devil established.

choices.why: Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
